articleTitle: A 5 to 25GHz Four-Way Power Combined Low Voltage Driver Amplifier Robust to Radiation, Temperature, Process and Aging
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This work presents an ultra-compact and broad-band power amplifier operating from 5GHz to 25GHz with a peak output power of 21.6dBm. This performance is thanks to the combination of an ultra-broadband digital distribution network and a broad-band series power combining network. By avoiding any band limiting electromagnetic coupling networks until the critical last stage, this work accomplishes exceptional bandwidth in a compact size. Unlike previous works targeting high power, compact size and extremely broad bandwidth, this work accomplishes this performance without using high supply voltages. By avoiding the significant levels of voltage stacking used in prior art to accomplish similar performance levels, this design drastically improves PVT robustness. Finally, this device is characterized for satellite communication use, showing robustness to aging, temperature and radiation through Total Ionizing Dose characterization.

articleTitle: Physics-Based Modeling and Characterization of Wide GaN-HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: In this paper, we model and characterize an unconventionally wide GaN HEMT device. Each finger of the device has a width of $150 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ which allows the modeling methodology to examine the wave propagation effects at high frequency bands. The transistor simulation employs a hybrid model, integrating a simulator for the transport equations of the semiconductor device and an electromagnetic solver for the extrinsic components. By combining these two elements, we can achieve a more comprehensive and accurate simulation of the transistor’s behavior. To assess the accuracy of our modeling technique, we compare the current gain predicted by the model with experimental measurements. The results demonstrate that our model is capable of accurately tracking the reduction in gain at frequencies beyond 50 GHz, highlighting its effectiveness in predicting high-frequency performance.

articleTitle: Impact of Temperature-dependent Emission Time Constant of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on DPD with Trapping Effects Compensation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of temperature-dependent emission time constant in AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on DPD with trapping effects compensation. Experimental results conducted on a GaN power amplifier reveal that different emission time constants are required to achieve optimal performance at different temperatures. Considering the significant impact of temperature-dependent emission constant on linearization performance, there is a clear need for advanced algorithms capable of adapting to real-world operational environments characterized by dynamic traffic loads and ambient temperature variations.

articleTitle: K/Ka-Band Eight-Way Power-Combined Power Amplifier in 180 nm E-Mode GaAs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: In this work, the design of a broadband K/Ka-band Power Amplifier (PA) Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) in 180 nm E-mode GaAs pHEMT technology is discussed. In small-signal the design has a flat frequency response from 23.8 GHz - 28.7 GHz covering a fractional bandwidth of 19.2%, with a maximum gain of 34.9 dB at 25.5 GHz. On top of that, the PA has a maximum output power of 28.5 dBm and a maximum Power-Added Efficiency (PAE) of 20.6%.

articleTitle: Low-Complexity Sequential LMBA for FR1 5G NR
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents the design and characterization of an SLMBA targeting 10-dB back-off efficiency enhancement in the N78 ($3.3-3.8 \mathrm{GHz}$) 5 G band. The design aims at minimizing complexity by adopting identical transistors in all branches and the same drain supply voltage. The prototype delivers more than 44dBm saturated output power while maintaining efficiency higher than 56% and 34% at saturation and 10 dB back-off, respectively. This confirms the validity of the approach in providing performance in line with the current state of the art.

articleTitle: An On-Die Diode-Based Temperature Sensor in GaN without Device Characterization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: A method for on-chip temperature characterization of GaN MMICs is presented in this work. The diode is driven with a square wave of current, and the output is measured as the voltage across the junction. Because of the diode current-voltage relationship, this approach eliminates the need to characterize the saturation current of the fabricated device. An estimate of temperature is therefore available without extensive up-front characterization, offering a straightforward option for monitoring die temperature in reliability and self-test of wide-bandgap devices. The technique is demonstrated in a 120-nm GaN process over a 5°C to 90°C temperature range.

articleTitle: Broadband H-Band Power Amplifier with Optimum Intermediate Splitter and Combiner Impedance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper reports the successful application of an optimum intermediate impedance in the splitter/combiner structure between the parallelization paths of a five-stage common-source amplifier design to achieve a broadband power amplifier. The amplifier has a record S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> bandwidth of 84 GHz between 226 and 310 GHz. This conventional common-source design is competitive regarding bandwidth with inherent broadband H-band traveling-wave amplifiers but offers a larger maximum gain of 19.9 dB. An $\mathrm{OP}_{1 \mathrm{~dB}}$ of more than 8.2 dBm is measured at 243 GHz, while exceeding existing common-source designs by 27 GHz in small-signal bandwidth.

articleTitle: A 77-GHz Power Amplifier in a 90-nm GaN Process
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a three-stage 77-GHz MMIC PA in a 90-nm GaN process under development. Only a single device-size non-linear model was available and no device scaling allowed. Resulting in a limited staging ratio of 1:1:2, four $\mathbf{8} \times \mathbf{5 0} \mu \mathrm{m}$ HEMTs are used for two drive stages and an output reactively power-combined stage. Small-signal measurements show 7.1 dB of gain, which is about a 4 dB degradation compared to simulations. Due to the drop in gain and limited available power, the peak PAE and power could not be reached in measurement. Two PAs are cascaded by wire-bonds to compensate for limited available drive power. Measured large-signal performance for the cascaded amplifiers at $P_{{in }}=9 \mathbf{d B m}$ shows $P_{{out }}=22.5 \mathbf{d B m}$, a large-signal gain of 12.78 dB and $P A E=2.5 \%$. The chip layout with 6 individual PAs allows for additional off-chip power combining.

articleTitle: A 70W dual-band high efficiency MMIC Doherty PA linearized over 200MHz iBW for 2.3-2.7GHz macro base station driver applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an integrated Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) using 28V Silicon laterally-diffused metal-oxide semiconductor (Si-LDMOS) technology to address 3GPP-B40 (2300-2400MHz) and B41 (2496-2690MHz) bands for macro base station driver applications packaged in a 7x12mm2 in Power Quad Flat No-lead (PQFN). The design approach and achieved results are described. To meet the targeted specification in terms of bandwidth and efficiency requirements, an asymmetric 3-way DPA topology is adopted. Using digital predistortion (DPD), this device can achieve an adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) of -61 dBc for a 2c-5th Generation New Radio (5GNR) 10 MHz at 8 dB peak-to-average ratio (PAPR) signal at 36 dBm corresponding to 12.5 dB output back-off (OBO) from 48.5 dBm of P1dB (output power at 1dB gain compression) of 100MHz and 200MHz instantaneous bandwidth (iBW) for band B40 and B41 with an high efficiency of 29% for 30dB of gain thanks to the adopted architecture.

articleTitle: Simplified Real-Valued Time-Delay Neural Network for Compensation of Power Amplifier Impairments
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper proposes using a cascade of a static nonlinear system and a neural network for power amplifier behavioral modeling and compensation. The results demonstrate that the proposed model provides a better performance-to-complexity trade-off than the current state-of-the-art augmented real-valued time-delay neural network (ARVTDNN) method. When tested with a 64 quadrature amplitude modulated long-term evolution signal with 20 MHz bandwidth and 10.5 dB peak-to-average power ratio at 9.4 dB output back-off on a Doherty-like power amplifier operated at 2.35 GHz, the proposed model achieves an error vector magnitude (EVM) 36.1 dB and adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) of -45.1 dBc. Compared to ARVTDNN, it improves EVM by 2.2 dB and ACLR by 0.4 dB, with a 22% reduction in running complexity.

articleTitle: Robust Digital Pre-Distortion Parameter Estimation with Interpretable Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: Batch estimation using Least Squares (LS) is commonly used to calculate DPD coefficients. However, non-orthogonal polynomial-based structures in DPD lead to multicollinearity, causing ill conditioning in coefficient calculation. This paper introduces an improved Ridge Regression technique for digital pre-distortion (DPD) parameter reduction. Using Ridge Leverage, we identify DPD basis functions with minimal impact on linearization performance, achieving a 39% reduction in DPD coefficients.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Network based Digital Predistortion Linearization for 6G Joint Communications and Sensing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: Advanced digital predistortion (DPD) linearization systems have been the cornerstone of successful and energy-efficient base station deployments, particularly when the radio frequency power amplifier (PA) is pushed to operate near its maximum power ratings to achieve high wireless capacity and provide new service features. In this work, we explore how machine learning (ML) techniques can be effectively incorporated into the design methodology of PA linearization for the emerging 6G use case, namely joint communications and sensing (JCAS). Our experimental results indicate that adopting a generative adversarial network for ML-based DPD model parameters extraction consistently yields better adjacent channel leakage power ratios and normalized mean square errors for different JCAS waveforms compared to the adaptive moment estimation method using a mean squared error loss function. Moreover, this improvement is achieved using less training data, resulting in shorter convergence times to reach a certain level of linearity performance.

articleTitle: 10-16 GHz High Efficiency Power Amplifier MMIC Using GaN HEMT for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: The sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication is emerging by exploring the Frequency Range 3 (FR3) band, spanning from 7 to 24 GHz, i.e., the centimeter-wave (cm-Wave) band. This article presents a two-stage GaN MMIC power amplifier (PA) operating in the upper-mid range of FR3. A transmission-line-based output matching network is designed to achieve continuous Class-B/J operation, ensuring high efficiency over a wide bandwidth. The fabricated PA chip attains a saturated power-added efficiency ($\mathrm{PAE}_{\mathrm{sat}}$) of 34.6-45.9% with an output power ($\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{sat}}$) of 35.1-36.7 dBm from 10 to 16 GHz. At 12 GHz, when tested with a 122.88 MHz 64-QAM signal with a peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of 7.12 dB, the PA achieves an average output power ($\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{avg}}$) of 31.4 dBm, an average PAE ($\mathrm{PAE}_{\mathrm{avg}}$) of $\mathbf{2 8. 0 \%}$, an $\mathrm{EVM}_{\mathrm{rms}}$ of -26.9 dB, and ACPRs of -35.0/-37.8 dBc. With a 100 MHz 12.83 dB PAPR 64-QAM 5G NR signal, it achieves a $P_{\text {avg }}$ of $30.6 \mathbf{d B m}$ and a $P A E_{a v g}$ of $\mathbf{2 5. 7 \%}$, with ACPRs of -28.2/-31.0 dBc.

articleTitle: ANN Versus Cascaded Behavioral Models for DPD Linearization of Wideband Dual-Input PAs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper offers a thorough comparison of two families of digital predistortion (DPD) behavioral models used for the linearization of high-efficiency dual-input wideband power amplifiers. Specifically, N-stage cascaded (CC) models are compared with artificial neural networks (ANNs) models in terms of linearization performance and computational complexity. The DPD models are designed balancing the competing demands of linearity, output power, and power efficiency of a pseudo-Doherty load-modulated balanced amplifier (PD-LMBA), while also considering the complexity of the model. Experimental results using a 5G new radio test signal with 200 MHz instantaneous bandwidth demonstrate the potential benefits of CC and ANN behavioral models to linearize a high-efficiency PD-LMBA at an RF frequency of 2 GHz, delivering a mean output power level of 40 dBm at around 50% power efficiency.

articleTitle: A 15 GHz Stacked GaAs Power Amplifier For Potential 6G Application
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage stacked power amplifier designed at 15 GHz with 24.1 dBm output power, and 25.8% power-added efficiency (PAE) based on the WIN semiconductors 0.18 um GaAs technology. The power amplifier (PA) consists of a driver PA and a stacked cell amplifier. The stacked cell, which includes a common gate (CG) transistor and a common source (CS) transistor is designed to increase the voltage swing to deliver higher output power than a single transistor. A shunt capacitor and inductor are designed between the CG and CS transistors for equal voltage swing. The chip size is $2.5 \times 1.5 \mathrm{mm}^{2}$

articleTitle: A Variable Envelope Outphasing Concept for Transmitter Linearization
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: Outphasing transmitter is typically implemented by dividing amplitude-varying waveform into multiple power amplifier (PA) paths with zero peak-to-average-power ratios (PAPR) per path. This arrangement provides linear output for the combined signal with high amplifier efficiency. However, due to the combining of outphased signals, the output power of the combined signal is compromised. In this paper, we present a novel concept called variable envelope outphasing (VEOP), which allows the possibility of systematically distributing the time-varying amplitude of the signal to the common and outphasing parts. This provides a valuable tool to balance the linearity and output power and thus produce a high-PAPR signal as a sum of lower PAPR signals. The proposed VEOP concept is demonstrated through conductive measurements at 2.4 GHz. The experimental results show that the choice of PAPR distribution before and after the amplification stage through VEOP provides linearity and achieved output power trade-off.

articleTitle: Understanding memory and nonlinearity impact on the structure of Volterra series covariance matrices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: The regression of Volterra series models in the field of power amplifier modeling and digital predistortion requires the calculation of the model covariance matrix. Traditionally, this covariance matrix is attained by using sample estimators, resulting in a high number of operations and significant computational complexity. In this paper, we exploit the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signal model as a Gaussian random process to obtain the population estimators, thereby avoiding calculation from signal samples. This procedure is applied to memory and nonlinear effects by calculating the covariance matrices of an equalizer and a polynomial model. Results show that covariance matrices are shaped by the signal power, its oversampling, and the model structure. Further validation results in a digital predistortion scenario demonstrate that replacing the sample-estimated covariance matrix with population estimators provides equivalent performance while significantly reducing the number of operations in the calculation.

articleTitle: Strategies for tackling numerical issues in coefficient selection algorithms for Volterra models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: Coefficient selection techniques play a crucial role in the use of high-performance reduced-complexity Volterra models for power amplifiers (PAs) and digital predistortion. When these algorithms are used to obtain a sorted set of the most important regressors for the model, a common issue arises: modeling errors tend to rapidly escalate when the number of coefficients is very large. This work proposes several strategies aimed at mitigating this numerical effect. The numerical problems associated with coefficient selection techniques are studied by examining their underlying causes, proposing several strategies to address these issues. They are successfully tested for the modelling of the optimally predistorted 100-MHz signal provided by the iterative learning control approach for a Doherty PA.

articleTitle: Towards System-Level Modeling of Broadband Sub-THz Amplifiers for Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper reports on the initial system-level modeling of the non-linear behavior of an H-band power amplifier, looking towards ultra-broadband wireless applications. Based on small-signal as well as large-signal continuous-wave measurements, polynomial as well as Rapp models are extracted for a carrier frequency of 280 GHz, accounting for AM-AM and AM-PM distortion due to amplifier compression. System-level simulations are carried out to predict the signal degradation in terms of error vector magnitude for 1 GBd 64-QAM signals. Measurements obtained using a VNA-based cross-domain measurement platform demonstrate novel characterization capabilities under broadband-modulated conditions and confirm the correct modeling of the compression behavior. However, it is already indicated that models that do not account for the frequency dependency of its parameters are no longer suitable for accurate prediction under ultra-broadband signal conditions.

articleTitle: Study of Gain Compression Bandwidth on Power Amplifier Linearization Performances for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to estimate the impact of a Doherty power amplifier (DPA) Amplitude to Amplitude (AM-AM) deviation along the band on its linearizability using digital predistortion (DPD) system. The DPD system is simulated by replacing the power amplifier with its nonlinear impulse model that is extracted from continuous-wave (CW) simulations. The dataset is modified to reduce and increase only the AM-AM dispersions over the band. This technique and linearization performances are evaluated using a Monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) 75W 3-ways DPA at 3600MHz. During the power amplifier (PA) design phase, these simulations allow to quickly advise the designer of the maximum AM-AM deviation that the DPD system will be able to compensate for. The designer will tune the PA elements to maximize the efficiency-linearity trade-off.
